family.description: Coenzyme F420 is a hydride carrier cofactor that functions during methanogenesis. This family of proteins represents CofC, a nucleotidyl transferase that is involved in coenzyme F420 biosynthesis. CofC has been shown to catalyse the formation of lactyl-2-diphospho-5'-guanosine from 2-phospho-L-lactate and GTP [[cite:PUB00045885]].

causal_graphs.family_mapping: TableS3 WP_041753721.1,216aa,HKI454 equals E5ASS2 sequence1 residues6-221. PF01983 reference20-206 transfers to15-201. causal_graphs.limitations: These are relative fractions in coupled reactions, not absolute activity, binding affinity or an isolated-domain mechanism. S162T,C95A,M91A,H145A/H145T retain mostly3PG profiles. S162G retains detectable3PG; no universal zero or double-mutant synergy is inferred. Folding, abundance and partner effects are not independently excluded.

record.description: Coenzyme F420 is a hydride carrier cofactor that functions during methanogenesis. This family of proteins represents CofC, a nucleotidyl transferase that is involved in coenzyme F420 biosynthesis. CofC has been shown to catalyse the formation of lactyl-2-diphospho-5'-guanosine from 2-phospho-L-lactate and GTP [[cite:PUB00045885]].

evidence.explanation: TableS3 RefSeq sequences resolve the Mrhiz five-residue offset; TextS2 pMH43 translates exactly to the B3 structure construct. Fo units and absolute mutant activities remain unresolved.
Figure2 supports paired product formation; the exact synthetic insert, incubation endpoint and supplemental no-partner controls were not fully audited.

discussions.notes: See evidence/PF01983/identity-and-coordinates.txt and the two primary-source ledgers. Paper Mrhiz S162 maps to E5ASS2 S167. B3 is not sequence-identical to E5ASS2, and MJ1117 is not MJ0887. Model contacts, channeling and folding-independent mutant mechanisms are not observed edges.
